newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Equity trade scattered.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Equity trade scattered.

text.p: Individual equity options trading Thursday was not focused on any one sector or group, as various strategies were exercised in different groups.

Traders said Morgan Stanley was the driving force behind some of the largest trades, specifically in Citicorp options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange and in Noble Drilling Corp on the New York Stock Exchange.
More than 4,000 of the Noble March 20 calls changed hands and traders said Morgan was in buying for a customer. The volume crossed in two blocks of 1,000 contracts, two of 900 and two of 100.
Noble shares were up 3/8 at 19 in afternoon trading on Thursday.
The only other busy Noble option was the January 17-1/2, which traded 1,000 contracts and crossed in one block.
Traders said Morgan Stanley sold 3,000 of the Citicorp July 100 puts for 5-3/4 and also were sellers of the January 65, 70 and 75 puts.
The January 65 put traded about 3,000 contracts and the 70 and 75 puts traded 1,120 and 1,000 contracts, respectively.
The January 65 puts and July 100 puts went out as a spread, as did the January 70 and 75s.
"Morgan crossed it all," one trader said. "The crowd traded none."
Another high volume situation was seen in options on shares of Galoob Toys Inc, where the December 35 calls and puts each traded about 2,000 contracts.
One trader said the volume was a reversal conversion in which the investor would have sold stock, sold the puts and bought the calls.
A regular conversion, in which an investor buys stock, buys puts and sells calls, establishes a synthetic call position.
Galoob shares were down 2-3/4 at 27-1/4 in afternoon trading.
Elsewhere, Barrick Gold, which had the most active options on Wednesday, saw heavy trading in the January 30 calls, with more than 3,800 contracts changing hands.
The Barrick January 25 put and April 25 put each traded more than 10,000 contracts Wednesday.
Barrick shares rose 7/8 to 29-7/8, extending Wednesday's sharp gains.
Two LEAPS (long-term equity anticipation securities) on shares of Philip Morris Cos Inc traded on heavy volume, mostly from a spread.
The January 1998 100 call traded about 2,550 contracts and the January 1998 110 call traded about 2,440.
Of that volume 2,181 contracts in each crossed as a spread.
Philip Morris shares, which rallied Wednesday, were ahead another 2-21/32 Thursday afternoon.
